new.title: Join a craft workshop at Ulucanlar Sanat Sokağı
new.desc: Altındağ Municipality runs an art street inside the former Ulucanlar semi-open prison grounds, where resident artists teach traditional crafts. The monthly programme has included ebru (marbling), çini tile painting, keçe (felt), calligraphy, glassblowing and copper relief workshops.
new.tip: Sessions have age limits and small quotas, so book through Altındağ Belediyesi (0312 507 01 30) before going.
new.q: Ulucanlar Sanat Sokağı, Ulucanlar Cezaevi, Cumhuriyet Mahallesi, Altındağ, Ankara

new.title: Browse handmade crafts at the Hamamönü El Ürünleri Pazarı
new.desc: The Altındağ Municipality hand-products market in Hamamönü gives women producers two halls to sell handmade jewellery, decorated clothing and souvenirs. It sits among the restored Ottoman houses of the Hamamönü quarter.
new.tip: Combine it with a walk along Hamamönü's restored streets; opening days are not published, so check with Altındağ Belediyesi.
new.q: Altındağ Belediyesi El Ürünleri Pazarı, Hamamönü, Hacettepe Mahallesi, Altındağ, Ankara

new.title: Catch a play at the Oda Tiyatrosu in Ulus
new.desc: Oda Tiyatrosu is a small stage of the Turkish State Theatres in the Evkaf Apartmanı in Ulus, the same building as the State Theatres head office. It stages works by Turkish playwrights.
new.tip: Plays are in Turkish; check the Devlet Tiyatroları programme and buy tickets in advance.
new.q: Oda Tiyatrosu, II. Evkaf Apartmanı, İstiklal Caddesi, Ulus, Altındağ, Ankara

new.title: See a State Theatres production at the Küçük Tiyatro
new.desc: The Küçük Tiyatro is one of the Ankara State Theatres stages in Ulus, housed in the Evkaf Apartmanı building that also holds the Oda Tiyatrosu and the General Directorate of State Theatres. Ankara is the home of the Turkish State Theatres tradition.
new.tip: Check the Devlet Tiyatroları site for the programme; the Ulus metro stop is the closest.
new.q: Ankara Devlet Tiyatrosu Küçük Tiyatro, İstiklal Caddesi, Ulus, Altındağ, Ankara

new.title: Watch a play at Gençlik Parkı Şehir Tiyatroları
new.desc: The Ankara Metropolitan Municipality's city theatre stages in the Gençlik Parkı Kültür Merkezi were renovated and host seasons such as the Gençlik Parkı Tiyatro Buluşmaları. It is a rare chance to see Ankara's independent and city companies in one place.
new.tip: Tickets are sold at the Gençlik Parkı Kültür Merkezi box office or online; check the current programme first.
new.q: Gençlik Parkı Kültür Merkezi, Gençlik Parkı, Anafartalar Mahallesi, Altındağ, Ankara

new.title: Make your own toy at the Ankara Toy Museum
new.desc: The Ankara Toy Museum was founded in 1990 by collector Şerafettin Yıldız and has been run by Altındağ Municipality in Hamamönü since 2017. Visitors can take part in a make-your-own-toy workshop.
new.tip: Fits well with a Hamamönü walk; ask at the museum about workshop times.
new.q: Ankara Oyuncak Müzesi, Hamamönü, Hacettepe Mahallesi, Altındağ, Ankara

new.title: Watch wooden toys being made on Hamamönü Sanat Sokağı
new.desc: A workshop on the Altındağ-renovated Sanat Sokağı in Hamamönü makes and sells traditional wooden toys, including Karagöz and Hacivat, Nasreddin Hoca and Keloğlan figures, in the Eyüp toymaking tradition. The maker is recognised as a UNESCO Living Human Treasure for wooden toy making.
new.tip: Visit in daytime when workshops are open; toys make good souvenirs.
new.q: Hamamönü Sanat Sokağı, Hacettepe Mahallesi, Altındağ, Ankara

new.title: Learn tragacanth doll making at Altınköy
new.desc: Altınköy Açık Hava Müzesi in Altındağ's Beşikkaya neighbourhood recreates a traditional Anatolian village, and local crafts such as kitre bebek (tragacanth dolls) are taught and made there. It is about 15 km from the city centre.
new.tip: Closed on Mondays; it is best reached by car or taxi, so confirm current hours with Altındağ Belediyesi.
new.q: Altınköy Açık Hava Müzesi, Beşikkaya Mahallesi, Altındağ, Ankara

new.title: Spot the cliff-side Alicin Monastery near Kızılcahamam
new.desc: Known locally as the Mini Sümela, the Alicin Monastery is a rock-cut structure high on a volcanic tuff cliff above the Alicin canyon. Its origin is uncertain and the site is classed as a geosite.
new.tip: Follow the Alicin geosite signs from Kızılcahamam towards Çeltikçi; the building itself is reachable only by experienced climbers, so view it from the canyon.
new.q: Alicin Manastırı, Alicin Kanyonu, Çeltikçi, Kızılcahamam, Ankara

new.title: Explore the Kızılcahamam Jeopark Müzesi
new.desc: Kızılcahamam Municipality opened its Jeopark Müzesi in March 2019, presented as a first for Turkey. It introduces the geology of the Kızılcahamam-Çamlıdere geopark, whose volcanic landscapes include the Abacı rock formations.
new.tip: Pair it with a visit to the Soğuksu thermal area; check opening hours with the municipality.
new.q: Jeopark Müzesi, Kızılcahamam, Ankara

new.title: See the petrified forest at Pelitçik in Çamlıdere
new.desc: The Çamlıdere Petrified Forest lies on Kuztepe hill by Pelitçik village, about 70 km north-west of Ankara. The fossil wood sits in lake sediments from the Early Miocene, some 23 to 15 million years ago, and the area is part of the proposed geopark.
new.tip: Go by car in dry weather; roads to the village are rural.
new.q: Çamlıdere Taş Ağaçlar Ormanı, Pelitçik Köyü, Çamlıdere, Ankara

new.title: Walk through Pazar village in Kızılcahamam
new.desc: Pazar is a village about 61 km north of Ankara with a former Roman-period church used as a mosque, old graves and the 19th-century Halil Ağa Mosque. Pazar Deresi runs through it.
new.tip: Take a car from Kızılcahamam; the stream and village paths suit a short morning walk.
new.q: Pazar Köyü, Kızılcahamam, Ankara

new.title: Walk to the Acısu mineral springs near Kızılcahamam
new.desc: Acısu Deresi, a stream about 4 km north-east of Kızılcahamam, carries mineral spring water at roughly 31 to 34 degrees Celsius. The Acısu and Seyhamam springs are cooler than the deep wells that feed the town's thermal hotels.
new.tip: Wear shoes that can get wet and ask locally for the path from town.
new.q: Acısu Deresi, Kızılcahamam, Ankara

new.title: Step into Beypazarı's Yaşayan Müze
new.desc: The Yaşayan Müze (Living Museum) in Beypazarı shows Ottoman-era home life and traditional crafts in a restored house. It is one of the stops visitors enjoy most in the historic town.
new.tip: Visit in the morning before the weekend crowds; it is a short walk from the bazaar.
new.q: Yaşayan Müze, Beypazarı, Ankara

new.title: Eat fresh gözleme at Kahyaoğlu Gözleme Evi in Beypazarı
new.desc: Kahyaoğlu Gözleme Evi is a village-style breakfast and gözleme place in Beypazarı's bazaar, a short walk from the town museum. The gözlemes are cooked in front of guests.
new.tip: Try the cheese-and-spinach or potato gözleme; go before lunchtime on weekends.
new.q: Kahyaoğlu Gözleme Evi, Beypazarı Çarşı, Beypazarı, Ankara

new.title: Have a village breakfast at Paşa Konağı, Beypazarı
new.desc: Paşa Konağı is a restored two-storey wooden house in Beypazarı's İstiklal quarter with a restaurant. It serves a village breakfast with local cheese, Beypazarı kurusu and Beypazarı simidi.
new.tip: Ask for the kuru and simit alongside the cheese plate; book if staying the weekend.
new.q: Paşa Konağı, Çakmak Sokak 4, İstiklal Mahallesi, Beypazarı, Ankara

new.title: Visit the Atatürk Çocukları ve Doğal Yaşam Parkı
new.desc: The Ankara Metropolitan Municipality opened this park on the Atatürk Orman Çiftliği grounds in Gazi, Yenimahalle, replacing the old AOÇ zoo. It spans roughly 940,000 square meters, and a 5,000 square meter digital zoo has been added.
new.tip: Weekends are crowded; check current hours and entry rules on the municipality site.
new.q: Atatürk Çocukları ve Doğal Yaşam Parkı, Atatürk Orman Çiftliği, Gazi Mahallesi, Yenimahalle, Ankara

new.title: See aircraft at the Ankara Aviation Museum
new.desc: The Ankara Hava Kuvvetleri Müzesi stands on the İstanbul Yolu in Etimesgut and opened on 18 September 1998. It is run by the Turkish Air Force and displays aircraft from the air force's history.
new.tip: Confirm opening hours and any ID requirement before going, since it is on a military site.
new.q: Ankara Havacılık Müzesi, İstanbul Yolu, Etimesgut, Ankara

new.title: Study the METU Faculty of Architecture building
new.desc: Altuğ and Behruz Çinici won the 1961 competition for the METU campus, and their Faculty of Architecture was the university's first building, completed so the university could move in on 1 October 1963. Its raw-concrete forms and pedestrian forum are landmarks of Turkish modernism, and the campus is treated as modern heritage.
new.tip: Walk in on a weekday during term; the building is part of the open campus.
new.q: ODTÜ Mimarlık Fakültesi, Üniversiteler Mahallesi, Çankaya, Ankara

new.title: Tour the Cumhurbaşkanlığı Millet Kütüphanesi
new.desc: The Presidential Nation's Library in the Beştepe presidential complex is open around the clock and is known for its Cihannüma Hall and Divan Hall as well as a children's library. It set a visitor record in February 2026.
new.tip: Entry is by QR code after e-Devlet membership; check the library's rules for casual visitors.
new.q: Cumhurbaşkanlığı Millet Kütüphanesi, Beştepe, Yenimahalle, Ankara
